title: GitLab Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in GitLab. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: What stores the project code history?
questions.explanation: A GitLab project contains a Git repository and related work tools. A group can organise several projects and their access in one place. The project is more than its files. Its related tools help track work and review changes around the repository.

questions.question: Which part is the project name here?
questions.explanation: A namespace is a path that helps locate a GitLab project. Groups and subgroups can add levels to that path. The path shows where the project is organised. Two projects in different namespaces can have the same final project name.

questions.question: What do labels help with?
questions.explanation: Labels mark kinds of work so issues can be filtered or grouped. A label should have a meaning the team understands. The labels help find related issues. They describe the work; they do not fix the problem or decide its priority by themselves.

questions.question: What ties these issues together?
options: They all need the same file name
questions.explanation: A milestone groups issues and merge requests around a goal or period. It helps show what work remains for that goal. The three tasks support one demo goal. Completing a milestone requires checking the intended outcomes, not only changing task labels.

questions.question: What does moving a card mainly communicate?
questions.explanation: An issue board shows work in columns based on chosen project rules, often using labels. It helps a team see items waiting or in progress. The card position communicates a work state. The team needs a clear meaning for each column so movement is useful.

questions.question: Which branch receives the proposed edits?
questions.explanation: A merge request, or MR, proposes combining a source branch into a target branch. It connects code changes with review and pipeline results. The source contains the proposed edit. The target receives it after the project's review and merge rules are satisfied.

questions.question: What makes this discussion ready to resolve?
options: The comment has been read once
A clear decision, change and check
questions.explanation: Review discussions can point to a specific line or behaviour. Resolving one should mean the concern has been addressed or an agreed decision has been recorded. The discussion leads to a clear behaviour and a check. The review history explains why trimming was added.

questions.question: What executes the job commands?
questions.explanation: GitLab CI/CD reads jobs from its pipeline configuration. A job names commands for a runner, which is the worker that executes them. This is a worked description of a job, not executable YAML. The runner needs a suitable environment with the project dependencies installed.

questions.question: Which two jobs could run in parallel here?
options: Build and its dependent checks before build finishes
questions.explanation: Stages can group pipeline jobs in an order such as build then test. Jobs in one stage may run in parallel when runners are available. The plan places build before the test stage. The two test jobs may run at the same time. Features such as needs can change dependencies in real pipelines.

questions.question: What is the artifact in this plan?
options: The name of the project group
questions.explanation: An artifact is a saved file from a job, such as a test report or built package. It lets later steps or reviewers inspect useful results. The report adds evidence beyond a green or red status. An artifact may contain sensitive data, so choose its contents and access thoughtfully.

questions.question: Why restrict direct pushes to main?
options: To remove the need for tests
To support the agreed review process
questions.explanation: A protected branch restricts who can push or merge. Merge checks can require useful conditions, such as a successful pipeline, before combining code. The plan combines access rules and evidence checks. Available settings vary by GitLab version, plan and project configuration.

questions.question: What does an environment record help identify?
options: Whether all future versions are correct
questions.explanation: An environment represents a place where an application runs, such as a preview or production site. A deployment record links a version to that place. The record identifies which version was put in which place. Our example is a written plan and does not deploy anything.
